analyzed_vuln.description: `xmlParseNCNameComplex` saves the name start as an offset from `ctxt->input->base`, then repeatedly calls `CUR_CHAR`, which can invoke `xmlParserGrow`. If that grow/conversion fails, `xmlBufUpdateInput` can replace `base`, `cur`, and `end` with the global empty-string buffer. The function does not detect this input-buffer change or halted/error state and later reconstructs `BASE_PTR + startPosition` using the stale offset, passing that invalid pointer and a positive `len` to `xmlDictLookupHashed`. `xmlDictHashName` then reads past the global empty string. The analogous complex Name parser already validates against unexpected input-buffer changes; the NCName path lacks equivalent validation.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The fuzz data defines an XSLT stylesheet containing `xsl:include`, causing libxslt's document loader to parse a fuzz-provided external entity. That included document declares a non-UTF-8 encoding (`Cp866`) and contains a malformed/non-ASCII start-tag QName, forcing the complex NCName path. While scanning that name near the available converted input boundary, `CUR_CHAR` requests buffer growth/encoding conversion. The allocation limit encoded in the first four fuzz bytes makes this operation fail, resetting the parser input pointers. A nonzero saved start offset and positive parsed-name length are then required so the stale reconstructed pointer lies beyond the global empty-string object and dictionary hashing performs the out-of-bounds read.
